Download People looking for affordable, flexible housing and residents living in Bury's neighbourhoods will benefit from new guidance adopted by Bury Council to support sustainable, inclusive growth across the borough The new Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMO) Supplementary Planning Document (SPD) recognises the important role HMOs play in providing accommodation for young professionals, key workers, people on lower incomes and those with short-term housing needs The guidance will help ensure future HMOs are well-designed and well-managed, supporting housing choice while protecting the character, wellbeing and balance of local communities The new SPD introduces clear planning criteria to help prevent excessive concentrations of HMOs. These include a 10% concentration threshold within a 100-metre radius, measures to prevent single-family homes from being “sandwiched” between HMOs, and restrictions on creating three At the same time, the SPD seeks to address concerns associated with poorly located or over-concentrated HMOs, such as parking pressures, noise, waste management issues and the loss of balanced communities

raw_evidence: The sister of a man who has been in prison for 14 years without a fixed release date, has welcomed government plans to review "inhumane" indeterminate sentences Thomas White was jailed for a minimum of two years in 2012 for the theft of a mobile phone. He was subject to an Imprisonment for Public Protection (IPP) sentence, with no maximum term and is still serving his sentence But after the Prime Minister asked for a review of Imprisonment for Public Protection (IPP) sentences on Monday , his sister Pastor Clara White said there is now hope in sight "My brother doesn't know if he will ever leave prison or die there," Clara said. "It's inhumane. But the review brings a light in the darkness." Intended for the perpetrators of serious crimes and persistent criminals, Imprisonment for Public Protection (IPP) sentences were introduced in 2005. And allowed judges to give out sentences with no maximum tariff to perpetrators of serious crimes or repeat offenders Deemed controversial IPPs were scrapped in 2012, but this was not retrospective. As of this year, more than 2,000 people are still in prison on IPP sentences according to the United Nations, (UN), who have called for the end of IPP sentences. , external

On April 30, 2010, Ron spent part of the afternoon in the Village with a friend belatedly celebrating his 32nd birthday Between 2pm and 3pm, he caught a train from Piccadilly Station to Northwich and would have arrived about an hour later. He then returned to the gay sauna he ran with his partner Ron was the manager of the venue - Sauna Sauna on Winnington Lane - and his partner owned it at the time. Many people find themselves avoiding photographs, covering their mouth when they laugh, or struggling to enjoy their favourite foods. It's easy to believe these changes are simply something you have to live with Unfortunately, the effects of tooth loss don't stop there. Over time, the jawbone can begin to shrink and neighbouring teeth may come under additional strain, potentially leading to further problems. Fortunately, modern dentistry offers a solution that looks, feels and functions A dental implant is a small titanium replacement for the root of a missing tooth. Once healed, a bespoke crown is attached, creating a replacement tooth virtually indistinguishable from the real thing Unlike dentures, implants are fixed securely in place - no slipping, movement or adhesives required. Unlike traditional bridges, they don't rely on neighbouring healthy teeth for support, helping to preserve natural tooth structure
